newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa forges higher despite strong stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa forges higher despite strong stg.

text.p: Cocoa futures forged higher by Wednesday midsession on short-covering and in a technical rebound to a sell-off earlier in the week.
Traders said cocoa's recovery was quite encouraging despite sterling's renewed strength against the German mark.
"It (the currency move) just effectively overshadowed the market," said one. "It probably detered the rally but the market did quite well despite sterling."
The September contract, which hit a four-month low of 968 stg on Tuesday, came back to finish at a session high 922 stg, a sharp 17 stg gain on the day, after gapping seven stg higher at the open.
Its low-point was 980. But analysts said the weak technical picture would not change until September regains a footing above 1,000 stg, seen as the immediate hurdle.

Sterling raced to top 3.0878 German mark, strongest since September 1989, on Wednesday morning before holding at 3.0770/80 at around midday in London. This compares with 3.0425/35 late Tuesday in Europe.
Traders said cocoa was poised for a correction after the sharp falls in the past few sessions.
"It is recovering on technical reasons more than anything else. The market was quite oversold anyway," the same trader said.
"Perhaps it is looking at the reversal given the lack of follow through on the downside," he said.
Traders called the New York cocoa futures to open $20 higher.
Fundamentally, traders said players remained uncertain about West African cocoa crop development.
Among latest crop news, Ivory Coast's dry season in July favoured drying of mid-crop cocoa (May-Sept) but will not damage pod growth for 1997/98 (Oct-April), analysts said.
Midday volume reached 1,822 lots. Options turnover was meagre at 25 lots.
